subject: Lumina SDK onboarding: local quickstart & test plan
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@lumina.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: SDK onboarding + local test plan for Lumina

Hi Alice / Lumina team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great alignment on the primary use cases (assistant routing + reranking for search + embeddings for semantic matching). Per our discussion, I captured the immediate next steps and a proposed local quickstart so your engineers can validate the integration end-to-end before we schedule the technical deep-dive.

Quick recap and asks:
- Primary flows: chat + structured tool-calls (webhook actions), embeddings for semantic search, and a lightweight reranker for top-k reordering.
- Auth: you mentioned SSO is important plus an API-key fallback for CI. Please confirm SSO provider (Okta/OneLogin) and whether we can use OIDC for service accounts.
- Routing: we should validate model routing rules (latency vs cost) and a fallback model for heavy traffic bursts.
- Data controls: Lumina asked about short-term retention for debug logs; our typical default is 30 days but can be adjusted on Dedicated/Private.

Local quickstart (what to try this week):
1) Python sample app (backend) — follows our quickstart (redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf attached): create virtualenv, pip install redwood-sdk, export REDWOOD_API_KEY (or point to an OIDC token), run sample_app.py which demonstrates chat + structured output.
2) TypeScript client (frontend) — clone the sample repo, npm install, set NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY locally, run next dev to test streaming responses and tool calls.
3) Embeddings + reranker smoke test — run embed_test.py against a small docset (script and expected outputs in lumina-mapping-sheet.xlsx).
4) Local-only auth test — mock SSO locally using a test OIDC token; we can provide a short checklist.

Attachments sent with this thread: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (step-by-step), lumina-mapping-sheet.xlsx (sample data + expected reranker labels).

Next steps:
- Alice: confirm SSO provider and whether a dedicated infra contact can join the deep-dive.
- Rishi / Engineering: can you prepare a minimal demo repo (Python + TS) with the structured output schema and a basic reranker hook?
- Marissa: I’ll follow up on commercial / PoC timeline once Lumina confirms scope.

I’ll set a follow-up for the deep-dive once we have the infra contact.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Laura / Alice — looping in a short tech plan for the local validation so Lumina’s infra team can hit the ground running. I kept it minimal so you can validate the critical pieces quickly.

Environment (recommended):
- Python: 3.11 in a venv (venv/.venv), pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0, pytest for smoke tests.
- Node: 18.x, yarn or npm, redwood-js client (npm i @redwood/inference-client).
- Docker: optional, but I added a small docker-compose stub in the repo to run a local redis for kv-cache and a mock tool-runner service.

Env vars we’ll use for local testing:
- REDWOOD_API_KEY (API key fallback)
- REDWOOD_OIDC_TOKEN (for OIDC test flows)
- REDWOOD_MODEL (default: redwood/gpt-small)
- REDWOOD_EMBED_URL (local test endpoint)

Local smoke commands (examples):
- python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
- python sample_app.py --mode=chat --mock-tools (starts on http://localhost:8080)
- cd web && npm install && npm run dev (frontend at http://localhost:3000)
- pytest tests/test_embeddings.py::test_basic_semantic_match

Structured output & tool calling notes:
- We'll include a JSON Schema for structured outputs (actions + params) in the demo repo. The Python sample_app will emit an action payload like: 
  {
    "action": "create_ticket",
    "params": {"summary": "..."}
  }
- Tool runner: simple webhook that validates schema and returns structured success/failure.

Embeddings / Reranker approach:
- Use batch embeddings (embed_test.py) to generate vectors for ~2k docs locally.
- Reranker: candidate generation via vector similarity (top-50) then a light transformer re-rank on top-10. We'll provide a small labeled set in lumina-mapping-sheet.xlsx for regression checks.

Testing tips:
- Mock out network calls with VCR/requests-mock when running unit tests.
- Use a local tiny model variant (redwood/gpt-tiny) for iteration speed.
- KV cache: run redis locally and point REDWOOD_REDIS_URL to redis://localhost:6379 to validate token reuse across steps.

I attached a short checklist I used for internal pilots (rishi-local-checklist.txt) and will push the demo repo to GitHub tonight at the link Laura mentioned.
